solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Courage reportedly iron?

indicators.note: reportedly tells us to go by how a word is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: iron is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: A question whether bravery is somehow made of iron, as in 'nerves of steel'.
explanation.walkthrough: Iron is a metal; 'reportedly' says the word wanted only sounds like that one.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit or resilience in the face of difficulty, so a direct synonym for courage.

clue.text: One producing notes for notes?

parts.note: suggests someone writing memos or banknotes for money, but the notes are musical ones played for a fee

explanation.surface: Sounds like a forger turning out banknotes, or a clerk writing memos for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'notes' is money: a player is paid notes for producing musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer of music produces musical notes, here in return for banknotes as payment.

clue.text: Prepare to protect monarch's land area

indicators.note: to protect means one word wraps around the other, guarding it

parts.note: to prepare someone is to train them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's standard monarch

explanation.surface: An instruction to get ready to defend the king's or queen's territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare' reads as the instruction but supplies the outer piece; the 's of monarch's is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of ground considered for its physical features, so a tract of land.

clue.text: Navy, no longer having case to be stationed in shelter, depart

indicators.note: to be stationed in says one piece is posted inside another

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, so they are dropped

explanation.surface: Sailors, no longer needing kit cases on a sheltered posting, set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Navy' looks like the subject, but it is only raw letters; 'shelter' is a noun, the lee of a wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To go away from a place is a plain synonym of set off.

clue.text: Second dish or some liquid?

parts.note: a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: A waiter asking whether a second course will be a dish or something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: a splash of fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Spattered drops or a splash of fluid, hence some liquid flung about.

clue.text: Easy progress in scheme to house one son — invalid

indicators.note: to house means to contain, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
one is the Roman numeral I
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
an invalid is unwell, ailing

explanation.surface: A care plan for housing a sick son that turns out to make things simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical idiom for smooth, trouble-free going, so progress without difficulty.

clue.text: One hostile to government Thracians reconstructed

indicators.note: reconstructed says the letters of the word are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Ancient Thracians, rebuilt by historians, as rebels against all rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer in abolishing the state is by definition opposed to rule by government.

clue.text: Capital journey on liner is just starting

parts.note: a journey is a trip

indicators.note: just starting picks the opening letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: A voyage to a capital city aboard a liner is just beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripoli is the capital of Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya, an example of a capital.

clue.text: Tree fern is too much for boat worker

indicators.note: is too much for says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gardening picture: a tree fern proves too much work for a deckhand.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters wanted are within 'Tree fern', from its second letter to the last but one.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor who takes in or lets out reefs in the sails, so a hand working on a boat.

clue.text: Joke about participating in trick

indicators.note: participating in means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a scam is a trick or swindle
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A gag concerning someone's part in a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is RE (as in a letter's 're:'), not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a hilarious person or thing is called this, a sense close to a joke.

clue.text: Lotion powder from California, a lucrative source

parts.note: a mine is a source of wealth, as in a gold mine

explanation.surface: A skin lotion's base powder sourced from a profitable Californian business.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink zinc-oxide powder used to make soothing skin lotions, so the powder for such a lotion.

clue.text: Get less manageable — intended, it's said, to bring about state of confusion

parts.note: to become wilder is to get less tame or manageable

indicators.note: it's said tells us to use the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: Things growing unruly, deliberately, so as to cause confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: BE WILDER read as a phrase is to get less manageable; 'to bring about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Total puzzlement or perplexity, a synonym for a state of confusion.

clue.text: One often changing drink meets writer at Christmas on return

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
the setter, the writer of the clue, refers to himself as me

indicators.note: on return means the word is read backwards

parts.note: Noel is another name for Christmas

explanation.surface: A fickle person who has a drink with a writer when they come back at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A lizard famed for altering its skin colour, so something that keeps changing.

clue.text: Almost equal in end

definitions.meaning: a near contest or result, nearly level
the conclusion or finish of something

explanation.surface: A contest that is nearly level right to the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a narrow, nearly level contest; the other is a finish, as of a day.

clue.text: Criminal ruins man's alibi for period — remarkable!

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook spoils someone's alibi, and that turns out to be quite something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun but signals the anagram; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for a wonderful year, a twelvemonth of extraordinary events, so a remarkable period.

clue.text: He follows US soccer played after first of September

indicators.note: after means the anagram comes after the picked letter
first of picks the opening letter of the word
played suggests the letters are rearranged, as in a game

explanation.surface: American soccer, played after the start of September, follows on from the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes over from another follows them in a role or line.

clue.text: Could be sweatier, so to speak

indicators.note: could be means the letters could become something else if rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that one might get sweatier, figuratively speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiomatic phrase meaning in a manner of speaking, a direct equivalent.

clue.text: Put on grief crier acted — so low, almost perverse

indicators.note: perverse means contrary or twisted, so the letters are twisted round
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A mourner putting on a show of sorrow, so base it is almost perverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims low to LO, which joins CRIERACTEDSO before 'perverse' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a hypocritical show of sorrow, so feigned or put-on grief.

clue.text: Take Two at Hollywood?

parts.note: in filming a take is one recording of a scene, and a second take means filming it again

explanation.surface: A film director calling for a second attempt at a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To film a scene again is exactly what a second take on a film set involves.

clue.text: Mediocre leader leaves party — anger follows

indicators.note: follows places the second piece after the first
the leader of a word is its first letter, and it leaves

parts.note: a rave is a party
rage is anger

explanation.surface: A political party loses a poor leader, and fury follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader leaves' drops the R of RAVE to give AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary, middling, of no special quality, so a synonym for mediocre.

clue.text: Vague talk, very loud in country, yet to finish

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
yet to finish means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: Wales is a country of the UK
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone droning on, loudly, about a country that has not finished something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet to finish' cuts WALES to WALE, which holds FF.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthy, empty, evasive speech is called this, a synonym for vague talk.

clue.text: Supermarket feature in Paisley

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A detail of a supermarket in Paisley, a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Paisley is a town in Scotland near Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of shelves is a feature of every supermarket.

clue.text: Becoming vigorous again, disregarding odds, urge on climb?

indicators.note: disregarding odds means ignore letters one, three and five, keeping the even ones

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: Revived, someone ignoring the odds urges on a climb.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'urge on' give REN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reborn or reviving after decline, so regaining vigour.

clue.text: Resort of French pack member

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A card belonging to a French holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four suits in a deck of cards, so a member of the pack.

clue.text: Old Labour leader's backing favourite for short distance

parts.note: Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983

indicators.note: backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A former Labour chief's support for a preferred candidate counts for little.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot was leader of Britain's Labour Party (1980-83). 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The length of one stride, so a very small distance.

clue.text: Container artist used in restaurant

indicators.note: used in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant
RA, Royal Academician, is the standard artist

explanation.surface: A vessel a painter used at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass flask for serving wine or water at table, a kind of container.

clue.text: Whole lot of virulent ire — typical!

indicators.note: of says the letters come from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A whole lot of venomous anger, and so characteristic of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The total or the whole of something, so the whole lot.

clue.text: Harsh energy cut earlier

indicators.note: earlier says the cut comes before energy

parts.note: to sever is to cut
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A severe power cut that happened earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern, strict or grim, a direct synonym for harsh.
